column2: “KARP 101 is clear to area one via the UNION departure. Runway heading up to 7, expect 9 to 230, 10 minutes after departure. Departure button four, squawk 4230.”  ⟶  Response: “KARP 101, readback correct.”  |  McCain Clearance Delivery (Pri)  |  CNATRA Ground Ops video (McCain)

column1: What do you say over the radio calling McCain Ground for taxi?
column2: “McCain Ground, KARP 101, single, taxi with information Charlie.”  ⟶  Response: “KARP 101, ground, taxi 1 right via Alpha Bravo.” → you: “101, taxi 1 right via Alpha Bravo.”  |  McCain Ground (Pri)  |  CNATRA Ground Ops video (McCain)

column1: What do you say over the radio calling Base out of chocks at McCain?
column2: “Base 01, out of chocks.”  ⟶  Response: “Have a good flight.”  |  Base (Aux)  |  CNATRA Ground Ops video (McCain)

column1: What do you say over the radio after landing at McCain, calling Ground?
column2: “(McCain Ground), KARP 101, single, clear the active, taxi my line.”  ⟶  Response: “KARP 101, ground, taxi to the line via Alpha.” → you: “101 to the line via Alpha.”  |  McCain Ground (Pri)  |  CNATRA Ground Ops video (McCain)

column1: What do you say over the radio calling Base after landing at McCain?
column2: “Base, 01, safe on deck.”  ⟶  Response: “Welcome back.”  |  Base (Aux)  |  CNATRA Ground Ops video (McCain)

column1: What do you say over the radio calling Maintenance for parking at McCain?
column2: “Maintenance, 01, in and up.”  ⟶  Response: “01, park Bravo.” → you: “01, park Bravo.”  |  Maintenance (Aux)  |  CNATRA Ground Ops video (McCain)

column1: What do you say over the radio when you lose two-way radio comms (any weather) — first action?
column2: Squawk 7600; try other freqs and transmit on Guard 243.0 / 121.5 (ATC will use Guard and NAVAID voice).  ⟶  Response: (ATC may transmit on Guard / NAVAID freqs)  |  Guard — 243.0 UHF / 121.5 VHF  |  NAV0102 Voice Procedures; NAV Gouge (INAV exam)

column1: What do you say over the radio when declaring a distress emergency?
column2: “MAYDAY, MAYDAY, MAYDAY” + station addressed, callsign/type, nature of emergency, weather, intentions, position/heading, altitude, fuel remaining, souls on board, other useful info — squawk 7700.  ⟶  Response: (ATC acknowledges, assists)  |  Current ATC frequency (else Guard 243.0 / 121.5)  |  NAV0102 Voice Procedures

column1: What do you say over the radio when declaring an urgency situation (not distress)?
column2: “PAN-PAN, PAN-PAN, PAN-PAN” + station, callsign/type, nature, weather, intentions, position/heading, altitude, fuel, souls, other info.  ⟶  Response: (ATC acknowledges)  |  Current ATC frequency (else Guard 243.0 / 121.5)  |  NAV0102 Voice Procedures

column1: What do you say over the radio when entering or leaving holding (not in the terminal radar/training exception)?
column2: Report “(callsign) entering holding / leaving holding” (exception: military terminal + radar contact + instrument training).  ⟶  Response: —  |  Current ATC frequency (else Guard 243.0 / 121.5)  |  NAV0102 Voice Procedures

column1: What do you say over the radio when picking up an IFR clearance after a VFR climb on course (NAV0103 example)?
column2: “Jacksonville Center, ROKT 21, VFR over Seminole at one zero thousand five hundred, looking to pick up my IFR flight plan to Navy Pensacola.”  ⟶  Response: (Center issues IFR clearance)  |  ARTCC (Center) frequency  |  NAV0103 Departure/Terminal

column1: What do you say over the radio when you are given an unacceptable clearance?
column2: Refuse it and state your reasons (“unable …”) — reading it back implies acceptance.  ⟶  Response: (ATC amends)  |  Current ATC frequency (else Guard 243.0 / 121.5)  |  NAV0102 Voice Procedures; NAV Gouge (INAV exam)
